results.title: Police repel suspected militants after attack in Mandera
results.description: File image of police officers on patrol in Mandera. Heavily armed militants launched a Sunday evening attack on Arabia town in Mandera County, sparking a fierce shootout with security forces who successfully repelled the invaders. Senior intelligence officials in Mandera confirmed that security personnel engaged the assailants in a heavy gunfight, ultimately forcing them to retreat. According to official reports, police officers and local security stationed in the border town managed to hold their positions and secure the area. While the identity of the gunmen has not been officially confirmed, officers suspected it to be Al-Shabaab militants, who have historically targeted towns along the volatile Kenya-Somalia border. Mandera senior police command stated that they have not yet recorded any casualties from the encounter. A comprehensive assessment is currently underway to determine the full extent of the incident, and security agencies have intensified patrols in the region to track down the fleeing attackers. ©Citizen Digital, Kenya

results.title: AMDA Emergency Relief #3: Earthquake in Colombia (7 September 2026)
results.description: Country: Colombia Source: Association of Medical Doctors of Asia Please refer to the attached file. In response to the devastating earthquake that struck Colombia last month, AMDA continues its relief activities in the disaster-affected areas in cooperation with AMDA Colombia and Fundación Salamandra, its local counterpart. On 2 and 3 September, the joint relief team traveled to Istmina, Chocó Department, in the country’s western region, where the earthquake’s epicenter was located. The team visited a hospital and a church in the city of Istmina for a needs assessment. As the team donated medical supplies including IV infusion sets during the hospital visit, its director explained that the facility remained operational although the earthquake had caused damage, tearing away part of its roof. In Istmina where building damage assessments had already been completed by the authorities, structures that were deemed unsafe were marked with "NO HAB" signs, indicating that entry was prohibited. Despite such circumstances, displaced residents were forced to take shelter in buildings at risk of collapse. Chocó Department was already facing economic challenges before the earthquake. This has raised concerns that certain obstacles could persist as the region moves towards recovery. The joint team is expected to respond to the needs on the ground further.
